title: NAPOLCOM probes 6 cops in alleged P1.2M Caloocan robbery
summary: The National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) has launched an investigation against six police officers who are implicated in a robbery incident involving P1.2 million worth of valuables in Caloocan City.

blocks.text: Published November 20, 2026 9:13am

The National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) has launched an investigation against six police officers who are implicated in a robbery incident involving P1.2 million worth of valuables in Caloocan City.

A complainant filed a complaint before the NAPOLCOM office on Thursday against six police officers, including the alleged mastermind, Police Major Jasper Benedict Santos, according to a report by GMA News’ Chino Gaston on Unang Balita.

NAPOLCOM said that according to the complainant, Santos of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) contacted him after learning that the complainant was selling a gold bracelet worth P700,000.
They agreed to meet on November 16 at a restaurant in Caloocan City, where Santos allegedly sent his driver and another companion to inspect the jewelry.
The complainant, who was accompanied by a police officer friend, was later instructed to proceed to another area to meet another supposed buyer.
Upon arriving, several armed men allegedly forced the two victims to lie face down on the road before taking them into a vehicle.

The complainant claimed the suspects staged an arrest by including another individual whom they supposedly had been monitoring and had just apprehended. He became suspicious when the individual was not handcuffed and appeared familiar with the armed men.
The complainant alleged that Santos was inside the vehicle, holding a firearm and pointing it at him.

He identified a police corporal as the driver and a former patrolman as another occupant. The ex-cop allegedly pointed a firearm at his face, while another unidentified man threatened him with a knife. The police corporal also allegedly threatened to kill him if he looked at the suspects.
The suspects reportedly took his gold bracelet, cellphone and firearm.

The complainant said the suspects later claimed that some of their belongings had been left on a motorcycle near a subdivision between Malabon and Valenzuela. However, they could no longer locate the bracelet, while the motorcycle was also missing.
NAPOLCOM said that the Philippine National Police (PNP) investigation also identified a police captain, a police senior master sergeant, and a patrolman as among those implicated in the incident.
Two unidentified individuals were also involved.
Santos, who was presented during the press briefing, denied the accusations and said he would explain his side before the court.

The complainant also disclosed that Santos's sibling had offered to replace his missing jewelry and other belongings, along with additional compensation, in exchange for dropping the complaint. He rejected the offer.
He also raised concerns about possible intimidation as unidentified individuals had been seen circling his residence.
Meanwhile, NAPOLCOM Commissioner Rafael Vicente Calinisan said the commission's investigation remains ongoing and would cover all individuals implicated.
Calinisan urged the remaining police personnel implicated in the incident to surrender voluntarily.
"Sa mga kasama ni Major Santos na hinahanap pa, sumuko na kayo. Hinahanap na kayo ng mga pulis. Huwag na ninyong pahirapan ang ating mga kapwa pulis na hulihin at arestuhin kayo," he said.

He called for stricter recruitment procedures, comprehensive background investigations and properly administered neuropsychological examinations to prevent individuals with questionable backgrounds from entering the police service.

"We have to remove the inept, corrupt, and undisciplined cops from the organization and ensure that those who will be recruited moving forward are qualified and committed to serving the public," Calinisan said. —VAL, GMA News
